turns.label: Clinician

turns.label: Patient

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Jerry is a 54 year old male with a past medical history, significant for osteoporosis and multiple sclerosis who presents for an annual exam. So Jerry, what's been going on since the last time I saw you?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, we have been traveling all over the country. It's been kind of a stressful summer. Kinda adjusting to everything in the fall and so far it's been good, but ah, lack of sleep, it's been really getting to me.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. All right. And have you taken anything for the insomnia. Have you tried any strategies for it.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I've tried everything from melatonin to meditation to, uh, t- stretching out every morning when I get up. Nothing really seems to help though.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. All right. In terms of your osteoporosis, I know we have you on fosamax, any issues with your joints, any issues like-

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: No broken bones recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: No, nothing like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. And then in terms of your multiple sclerosis, when was the last time you saw the neurologist?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, about six months ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay and you're taking the medication?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. And any issues with that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: None whatsoever.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And any additional weakness? I know you were having some issues with your right leg, but that seems to have improved or?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes a lingering issue with my knee surgery. But other than that it's been fine.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Pretty, pretty strong, n- nothing, nothing out of the ordinary.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. All right, well I know you did a review of systems sheet when you checked in.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Mm-hmm.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And you were endorsing that insomnia. Any other issues, chest pain, shortness of breath, anything?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: All right. Well lets go ahead and do a quick physical exam.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Mm-hmm.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Hey dragon, show me the vital signs. So your vital signs here in the office they look really good. I'm just going to listen to your heart and lungs and let you know what I find.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Sure.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. On physical examination everything looks good. You know your lungs are nice and clear. Your heart sounds good. You know you do have some weakness of your lower extremities. The right is about 4 out of 5, the left is about 3 out of 5. But you reflexes are really good so I'm, I'm encouraged by that. And you do have some, you know, arthritic changes of the right knee.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Mm-hmm.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Um, so let's go over some of your results, okay?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Sure.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Hey dragon, show me the right knee x-ray. And here's the x-ray of your right knee, which shows some changes from arthritis, but otherwise that looks good. turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Actually I do.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Hey dragon, order a refill of fosamax 1 tab per week, 11 refills. And then in t-, for your second problem, your multiple sclerosis I want you to go ahead and continue to see the neurologist and continue on those medications. And let me know if you need anything from that standpoint, okay?

turns.label: Patient
